diagram_name: Active Games and Dances Around the World
learning_objective: Students describe examples of cultural and traditional physical activities from different communities and compare what makes each one active and meaningful.
specification:
Type: map **sim-id:** cultural-physical-activity-map
**Library:** Leaflet
**Status:** Specified Bloom Taxonomy: Understand (L2) Bloom Taxonomy Verb: describe, exemplify, compare Learning objective: Students describe examples of cultural and traditional physical activities from different communities and compare what makes each one active and meaningful. Geographic scope: World map with five marked regions Purpose: Show that active, traditional games and dances exist in communities all over the world, each with its own history Locations and markers: - Philippines: Tinikling dance marker - North American Indigenous nations (general region marker, respectfully labeled by nation where possible): Powwow dance marker - West Africa: traditional circle-dance marker - Caribbean: jump-rope game marker (Double Dutch origins) - General "your community" marker inviting students to think of a local tradition Legend: Icons for "dance," "jump-rope game," and "group circle activity" Interactive features: - Click each marker to open an infobox with: name of the activity, a simple description, and one sentence on why it is physically active - All markers presented with equally respectful, neutral description style -- no marker described as more "unusual" than another - Button: "Show My Community" prompts students (via teacher discussion) to name a local tradition to add to the discussion Color scheme: Each marker uses the same neutral gold color (matching mascot palette) so no single tradition is visually emphasized over another Implementation: Leaflet map with custom marker icons and popups; simple world basemap with minimal extra detail so markers are the visual focus
